nodes.description: Private constant 86400 seconds-per-day used to round timestamps and compute the release schedule.
Immutable IERC20 token held and distributed by the timelock contract.
Immutable beneficiary address authorised to withdraw released tokens.
Immutable start timestamp (rounded down to a full day) of the token release period.
End timestamp of the release period; mutable and reset when the contract is terminated.
Total amount of benefit tokens reserved for the beneficiary; reduced on termination.
Amount of tokens already withdrawn by the beneficiary; updated on each withdraw.
Flag indicating whether the owner has terminated the timelock contract.
Owner address inherited from Ownable, used by the onlyOwner access control check.
Caller of the transaction reached through _msgSender(); untrusted input used for ownership and authorisation.
Current block timestamp, miner-influenceable input that drives the whole release schedule.
External low-level token call token().safeTransfer(_beneficiary, amount) executed in withdraw().
External low-level token call token().safeTransfer(owner(), amountToWithdraw) executed in terminate().
SupervisedTimelock constructor: stores token, beneficiary, release window and total benefit, and validates the end time against block.timestamp.
View function returning the held IERC20 token.
View function returning the beneficiary address.
View function returning the total benefit amount.
Time-dependent view function computing the vested amount from block.timestamp, the release window and _totalBenefit.
View function returning _totalBenefit minus the currently released balance.
View function returning the already withdrawn balance.
Withdraws the newly released tokens to the beneficiary; updates _withdrawedBalance then performs an external token transfer.
Owner-only function that caps the benefit at the released balance, freezes the release end time, marks termination and refunds the remainder to the owner.
Ownable view function returning _owner; used by the onlyOwner modifier and by terminate() as refund recipient.
Constructor parameter with the ERC20 token address held by the timelock.
Constructor parameter with the beneficiary address.
Constructor parameter with the requested release start timestamp.
Constructor parameter with the number of days of the timelock period.
Constructor parameter with the total amount of benefit tokens.
Local variable in releasedBalance holding the number of whole days elapsed since _releaseStartTime.
Local variable in releasedBalance holding the total number of days of the release window.
Local variable in withdraw holding the newly released amount to transfer.
Local variable in terminate holding the excess balance refunded to the owner.

edges.reason: Constructor parameter token_ is assigned to the immutable state variable _token.
Constructor parameter beneficiary_ is assigned to the immutable state variable _beneficiary.
Constructor parameter releaseStartTime_ is rounded down to a day boundary and stored in _releaseStartTime.
daysOfTimelock_ is multiplied by SECONDS_OF_A_DAY and added to releaseStartTime_ to compute _releaseEndTime.
Constructor parameter totalBenefit_ is assigned to _totalBenefit.
_releaseStartTime is combined with daysOfTimelock_ * SECONDS_OF_A_DAY to derive _releaseEndTime.
Constructor requires _releaseEndTime > block.timestamp, making deployment dependent on the timestamp input.
token() returns the _token state variable.
beneficiary() returns the _beneficiary state variable.
totalBenefit() returns the _totalBenefit state variable.
releasedBalance() branches on block.timestamp compared to _releaseStartTime and _releaseEndTime (timestamp dependency).
_releaseStartTime is read by releasedBalance() to compute the elapsed period.
_releaseEndTime is read by releasedBalance() to detect full release.
_totalBenefit is multiplied by passedDays and divided by totalDays when computing the vested amount.
SECONDS_OF_A_DAY is used by releasedBalance() to convert timestamp deltas into whole days.
_releaseStartTime is subtracted from block.timestamp to compute the passedDays local variable.
Local passedDays derives directly from the block.timestamp input.
_releaseEndTime participates in computing the totalDays local variable.
_releaseStartTime is subtracted from _releaseEndTime to compute the totalDays local variable.
Local passedDays feeds the multiplicative vesting formula inside releasedBalance().
Local totalDays acts as the divisor in the multiplicative vesting formula inside releasedBalance().
unreleasedBalance() subtracts the released amount from _totalBenefit.
unreleasedBalance() calls releasedBalance() to compute _totalBenefit - releasedBalance().
withdrawedBalance() returns the _withdrawedBalance state variable.
withdraw() calls releasedBalance() as the upper bound of the withdrawable amount.
withdraw() reads _withdrawedBalance to compute releasedBalance() - _withdrawedBalance.
withdraw() uses the _token state variable to query the balance and to transfer.
withdraw() uses the _beneficiary state variable as the transfer recipient.
The amount local variable takes releasedBalance() as its first operand.
The amount local variable subtracts _withdrawedBalance from the released balance.
withdraw() adds the computed amount to _withdrawedBalance (state update).
Local amount is the value argument of the external safeTransfer call in withdraw().
_beneficiary is the recipient argument of the external safeTransfer call in withdraw().
withdraw() transfers control to the token contract through the external safeTransfer call (unsafe operation).
A malicious or hooking token implementation can re-enter withdraw() during the external safeTransfer, before the transaction completes.
terminate() is guarded by onlyOwner, which compares owner() with _msgSender() (msg.sender); caller controls this input.
_owner is the reference value used by the onlyOwner authorisation check on terminate().
terminate() calls owner() for the access control check and as the refund recipient address.
terminate() checks the _isTerminated flag through the isNotTerminated modifier.
terminate() derives the new _releaseEndTime from block.timestamp, a timestamp-dependent value.
terminate() caps _totalBenefit at the value returned by releasedBalance().
terminate() overwrites the _totalBenefit state variable with the released balance.
terminate() sets _releaseEndTime to the day-truncated block.timestamp.
terminate() sets the _isTerminated flag to true.
terminate() queries the token balance of the contract to size the owner refund.
amountToWithdraw subtracts (_totalBenefit - _withdrawedBalance) from the contract token balance.
_withdrawedBalance participates in the nested subtraction that produces amountToWithdraw.
Local amountToWithdraw is the value argument of the external safeTransfer call in terminate().
_owner is read through owner() and used as the recipient of the terminate() refund transfer.
terminate() performs an external token transfer (unsafe operation) to the owner.
The external safeTransfer in terminate() can call back into the contract, enabling reentrant behaviour on the state of terminate().
owner() returns the _owner state variable.
Ownable's constructor initialises _owner from _msgSender() (msg.sender), the deployer-controlled input.

normalization_plan.reason: Constructor parameter token_ only exists to initialise the _token state variable inside the constructor.
Constructor parameter beneficiary_ only exists to initialise the _beneficiary state variable inside the constructor.
Constructor parameter releaseStartTime_ is rounded and immediately stored as _releaseStartTime inside the constructor.
Constructor parameter daysOfTimelock_ is only used inside the constructor to compute _releaseEndTime.
Constructor parameter totalBenefit_ only exists to initialise the _totalBenefit state variable.
Local passedDays is scoped and used only inside releasedBalance() to compute the vested fraction.
Local totalDays is scoped and used only inside releasedBalance() as the vesting divisor.
Local amount is scoped to withdraw() and is fully consumed by the state update and the external transfer.
Local amountToWithdraw is scoped to terminate() and is fully consumed by the owner refund transfer.
